story.what_it_does: Sarda Energy & Minerals is an integrated steel, ferro alloys, mining and power group. Power now brings in about two-thirds to three-quarters of its EBITDA, and the steel and alloy plants plus the coal mines make up the rest. FY2025-26 consolidated revenue from operations was ₹5,690 crore, with profit of about ₹1,103 crore.
story.plans: Management wants to double energy capacity to 1,200 MW and double EBITDA by FY30, and to expand coal mining and renewables. Near-term projects include a 50 MW captive solar plant, the Shahpur West coal mine and the Avagudem manganese mine. Annual capex of ₹500-700 crore is guided for FY27 and FY28, excluding the thermal expansion, which still needs approvals.
story.moat: The notes show some own-resource advantages: captive coal mines, hydro with a 40-year PPA at ₹7.42 per unit, and power that now drives most earnings. A new manganese mine is expected to cut raw material costs. The notes do not describe any other competitive edge, and steel and ferro alloy prices remain cyclical.

scenarios.story: Planned shutdowns end, thermal power is substantially higher in H2 FY27, and the solar, coal and manganese projects come on stream. The thermal expansion gets its clearances and EBITDA doubling by FY30 stays on track with a net debt-free balance sheet.
signals_to_watch: Thermal power generation in H2 FY27 versus the 420 crore units expected for FY27
Environmental clearance for the thermal expansion and SKS plant this financial year

scenarios.story: Earnings stay strong, led by energy, but are lumpy because of shutdowns and weak steel volumes. Management gives no FY27 guidance, and H1 FY27 EBITDA was a record ₹1,326 crore, up only 4%.
signals_to_watch: Return to a normal operating trajectory in Q2 FY27 and after
Steel billet, wire rod and sponge iron volumes, which fell sharply year on year

scenarios.story: The West Asia conflict raises input and logistics costs and weakens steel demand, and outages and one-time benefits mask weaker underlying profit. Pending approvals, disputes and a heavy dependence on one power customer could hurt results.
signals_to_watch: Energy Development Cess of ₹127.07 crore disputed at the Supreme Court, where orders are reserved
Share of revenue from the one major power customer, 31% versus 19% the prior year
